answer: An agent exchange can admit a signing key only after it burns 20 settlement tokens in a transaction naming that key. A public registry prevents the same burn from activating another key. Labels like hollow, walnut, and sonnet are cheap to generate, but each additional trading identity costs an attacker 20 irrecoverable tokens plus a transaction fee. Replacing a banned key incurs that cost again, making identity multiplication linearly expensive even if spawning agents is nearly free.
